messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 — unusual 401 surge vs management API (mgmt-api). source=edge-auth-proxy. Affected endpoint=/v1/keys. Pager: @maya-sre.

maya-sre: I'm on it. spike starts ~2026-03-18T02:12:10Z, ~50 distinct IPs, UA shows 'mgmt-probe/1.2'.

lucas-platform: I'm taking primary oncall. quick triage: check ingress logs, block offending IPs at edge, WAF rule for UA, consider rotating the mgmt service token if we see header leakage.

amira-security: adding sec oncall. I'll query s3 and ingestion logs for Authorization header exposures and check KMS CloudTrail for unusual decrypts.

maya-sre: logs snippet from prod-edge at 02:12:13Z:
```
time=2026-03-18T02:12:13Z src=54.23.12.9 method=POST path=/v1/keys status=401 ua="mgmt-probe/1.2"
```

lucas-platform: pushing temporary WAF rule to drop UA 'mgmt-probe/1.2' and block POST /v1/keys from the top ips. will roll to EU/US now.

ops-bot: WAF change applied: rule=r-892 (drop UA mgmt-probe/1.2), regions=[eu-west-1,us-east-1]. change_id=chg-202603180212. :white_check_mark:

amira-security: quick searches: grep over last 6h for "Authorization:" in s3 logs and edge logs. so far one match in staging (not prod) — pulling details. KMS audit shows no anomalous decrypts.

maya-sre: customer-impact: three enterprise customers reported failed key ops between 02:15–02:25Z. we're rate-limiting mgmt-api to reduce blast radius. no confirmed exfil, no S3 exposures in prod yet.

sara-product: drafting customer note. @maya-sre can you confirm list of affected customers and whether key rotation will break any scheduled jobs? need ETA for comms.

lucas-platform: plan for token rotate (low-risk rolling):
1) create new service token alias=mgmt-api-rot-01
2) update 10% of edge proxies canary
3) monitor 5m, if OK increment 10% every 2m
4) revoke old token once at 100%
I can run this.

maya-sre: executed edge blocks. starting token creation now. watchlist ips: [54.23.12.9, 18.201.45.6, 3.8.77.11]. KMS lookback shows normal activity for last 24h.

amira-security: ran content scan for 'Authorization: Bearer' across logs; result: 1 hit in staging-only CI artifact (path: s3://redwood-staging-logs/ci/2026-03-18/step-45.log). no prod hits. I'm escalating CI team to scrub that staging artifact.

dan-legal: keep comms factual. if we need to notify customers about leaks, legal wants to review draft before send. for now treat as mitigated but continue investigation.

maya-sre: token rotation progress: new token id tok-rot-20260318-1 created. rolling to canary (10%). updating config on canary proxies now.

lucas-platform: applied temporary rate limit 10r/s on /v1/keys for anonymous UAs; alert thresholds set: 5xx increase and sustained 401 rate > 5m.

maya-sre: 02:30Z check-in: 401s returned to baseline in both regions. WAF rule holding. token rotation at 40% with no errors. no evidence of data exfil.

sara-product: draft comms ready. message says: we observed elevated 401s to management API, mitigation applied (WAF + token rotation), limited customer impact (key ops for X customers intermittent). propose send window: 30m after we close. @dan-legal please review. :memo:

amira-security: follow-ups: (1) CI artifact scrub + rotate any credentials found in staging (2) add extra logging on mgmt-api to capture full UA + src ip for 72h (PII filter applied) (3) run deeper S3 scan run overnight.

dan-legal: reviewed draft, minor wording edits. ok to send after product finalizes recipients.

maya-sre: final status update: WAF rule still active, token rotate completed to 100%, old token revoked. monitoring for 1h. setting RCA timeline and next steps. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident -> mitigated, channel will be archived in 24h unless reopened. Post-incident actions: sec forensic, CI scrub, customer comms.
